The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 04.02.2019.
2.
The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 04.02.2019 at about 2.30pm the petitioner namely Manjunatha A.V. was working in his Agricultural land.
At that time one JCB vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-M-8574 was also carrying Agricultural work in the same land being operated by its Driver.
The petitioner was working cautiously by keeping safe distance from the said JCB.
The driver of the said JCB vehicle driven the same in a rash and negligent manner at SCCH - 25 3 MVC No.3870/2020 high speed.
As a result he lost control over his vehicle and the said vehicle went near the petitioner and one of its Wheel ran over petitioner's right foot.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Sri Gaurav Orthopedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar.

entities.text: Gaurav Orthopedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After first aid he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore in the said hospital X-rays were taken and clinical examination was done, he underwent surgeries i.e., wound debridement, K-wiring of right great toe and amputation of right great toe and treated as an inpatient and discharged from the hospital.
Thereafter till today the petitioner is under treatment as an out-patient.
So far he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, doing Agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the carelessness, rash and SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.3870/2020 negligent driving by the driver of the JCB vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-07-M-8574.
The Nangali Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.8/2019.
Therefore, the 1st respondent being the RC Owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
5. The objection of the respondent No.1.
He has denied all the petition averments except admitting that he is the RC owner of the JCB bearing No.KA-07-M-8574 and the same is insured with the 2nd respondent.
The policy of the vehicle is valid at the time of accident.
The said vehicle had valid insurance and driver is also having valid DL as on the date of accident.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
The objection of the respondent No.2.

It has denied all the averments of the petition except admitting the issuance of the policy in favour Manjunatha A.V vs Muniswamy Gowda K.N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119710520/
2 of the Respondent No.1 in respect of the JCB bearing KA-04-M-8574.

sentences.text: Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid DL as on the date of accident.
It has denied the manner of accident, age, income, medical expenses etc.,
It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

7. The objection of the Respondent No.2 in the Additional Written Statement It has submitted that,
the alleged accident occurred in Agricultural land situated at Survey No.14 at Bommadasanahalli Village, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District.
More particularly the alleged accident has occurred not in a public place.

Hence this respondent is not liable to indemnify the insured/Respondent No.1 towards such risk as it is a SCCH - 25 6 MVC No.3870/2020 private place and the same is in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of Driver of JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-M-8574 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
9. The Petitioner in order to prove his case has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.9.
Dr.Krishan Prasad got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.10 to 12.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision:
MFA No.6969/2015 C/w MFA No.6055/2015 : The Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt.Sunandamma and Ors.

 for the following:-
 REASONS  12. Issue No.1:-

sentences.text: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the SCCH - 25 8 MVC No.3870/2020 actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-07-M-8574, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.5.
He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination, he has stated that, at Ex.P.6 history shows that 'While walking in field with JCS' but it has to be JCB.
On the day of accident the JCB was leveling the land.
Further admitted that there was delay in lodging the complaint because his brother was alone in the hospital to look after him.
13. As per FIR at Ex.P.1, it was registered on 08.02.2019 after 5 days of the accident on the complaint of one A.V.Subramanyareddy - Brother of the petitioner at Ex.
P.2 . Ex.P.3 spot mahazar is in accordance with the statement given by the petitioner.
Ex. P.4
wound certificate shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries to right great toe while working in the land with a JCB on 04.02.2019 at around 2.30pm in Gudapally, Mulabagal Taluk.
The police SCCH - 25 9 MVC No.3870/2020 have conducted investigation and filed the charge sheet as per Ex.P.5 against the driver of the offending JCB.
The respondent No.2 has denied the manner of accident but did not prove the same.

All these documents show that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the JCB bearing Reg.No.KA-04-M- 8574.
14.
The respondent No.2 has contended that, the spot of accident was not a public place and it is not liable to pay compensation.

In support of the same the counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decision:
MFA No.6969/2015 C/w MFA No.6055/2015 : The Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt.Sunandamma and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that the expression 'right of access' in Sec.2(34) of MV Act includes any place to which the members of the public have access.

entities.text: Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt.Sunandamma and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The access may be permissive or limited restricted or regulated by oral or written permission, by tickets, passes or badges on payment of fee.
What is necessary is that the place must be accessible to the members of public and be available for their use, enjoyment, avocation or other purpose.
In the said case the Hon'ble High Court held that since the borewell drilling activity was carried out in the field of the defendant at 1.00am the field cannot be considered as a public place.
The court held that insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and fixed the liability on the owner.

As against this, the Counsel for the Petitioner has relied upon the following decision:
2024 ACJ 1244 (Kar) : Branch Manager, National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Kumari and Ors.
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that since public and farmers have access to Agricultural Lands it falls within the definition of public place.

entities.text: 2024 ACJ 1244 (Kar) : Branch Manager, National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Kumari and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Tractor driver going on the Road, suddenly drove the vehicle on the bunds of sugar cane field negligently.
15. In the case on hand, it is not in dispute that the accident took place in the Agricultural land belonging to the petitioner.
But it is pertinent to refer the decision of full bench of the Madras High Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Parvathi Devi And Ors.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Parvathi Devi And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Reported in 1999ACJ1520 SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.3870/2020 and the decision of a Full Bench of the Bombay High Court in Pandurang Chima-ji Agale v. New India Life Insurance Co. Ltd., 1988 ACJ 674, wherein it was observed as follows:
It is also necessary to bear in mind the distinction between the expression 'right of access' and 'access as of right'.

entities.text: Pandurang Chima-ji Agale v. New India Life Insurance Co. Ltd., 1988 ACJ 674
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The latter expression denotes a place where the members of public have a right of its use as members of public and as a matter of right, whether regulated, restricted or not.
They cannot, however, be denied the said right except on legal grounds.

On the other hand, where there is only a right of access,
the owner of the place, if he happens to be a private owner, may deny the access to any members of the public on any ground which he chooses.
In other words, in the former case, the right of the members of the public to use the place is restricted compared to their right to use in the latter case.
The definition under the Act uses the expression 'right of access' as pointed out earlier.
What is, therefore, significant to note is that under the present definition even a place the right to use of which is restricted is a public place.
Once this is borne in mind much of the controversy raised before us around the correct meaning of the expression 'public place' loses its edge.

Therefore, on combined reading of the decisions of full SCCH - 25 12 MVC No.3870/2020 bench of the Hon'ble Madras High Court and Hon'ble Bombay High Court it is clear that even a private place like a factory or agricultural land becomes a public place when the owner permits the public access to the place, leading to right of access to the public even though the said access is not as of right.
In the case of Sunandamma cited supra, the bore well was drilling at the time of 1.00am and therefore the place was not considered as public place.

Hence, by relying on the full bench decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras and Hon'ble High court of Bombay it is clear that the agricultural land of the petitioner is a public place with access to the public.
Therefore, the contention of the Respondent No.2 that the accident has not taken place in a public place is rejected.
16. The documents on record show that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the JCB.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by SCCH - 25 13 MVC No.3870/2020 the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.4.

As per this document, the petitioner got total amputation of right great toe at the level of IP Joint with IP joint dislocation (type open) & Loss of nail and germinal matrix (contaminated) & doubtful viability of tip which is grievous in nature.
18. The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Krishan Prasad as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.10 to 12 Out patient file (2 in Nos.), inpatient file (2 in Nos.) and X-ray with report.

He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed Near total amputation of the right great toe with IP joint dislocation with open type 3b crushing and contamination of the distal phalanx with loss of nail with doubtful vascularity.
Wound debridement was done with K- Wiring of great toe.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering disability of right lower limb disability at 34% and to the whole body at 12% and functional disability at 14%.
PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
He had not taken any written opinion from the treated Doctor.
Further admitted that first they tried to save the right big toe by inserting K wire but when it failed, they amputated it.
He can do desk Jobs but will be unable to do physically demanding walking jobs.

Disability:
20.
From the evidence of PW.2 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered whole body disability at 12% and the functional disability at 14%.
The petitioner has stated that he was doing Agriculture work.
But PW.2 has stated that the petitioner can do desk Jobs.
This means that he cannot do physically demanding walking jobs.
This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.
The Respondent No.2 has contended that the Loss of Earning capacity even under EC Act for loss of great toe is only 3%.
In support of the same, he has produced copy of the schedule to EC Act and referred Article 40.
But, Article 40 refers to SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.3870/2020 amputation of part of great toe with some loss of bone.
In this case, the petitioner has lost total amputation of great toe which is visible from the photographs at Ex.P.8.
This means that he will not have the grip to walk or to lift affecting his manual work in Agricultural land.
The schedule to EC Act Article 39 gives 14% disability to amputation of the great toe through metatarso-phalangeal joint.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 12% and functional disability at 14%.

Monthly income:
21.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Agriculture work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any Manjunatha A.V vs Muniswamy Gowda K.N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119710520/
6 documents like RTCs, Bank statement etc., to prove his earnings.

sentences.text: The accident occurred in the year 2019.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.14,000/- per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 43 years as could be made out from Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of DL.
He was hale and healthy before SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.3870/2020 the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Gourav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar and thereafter he was shifted to HOSMAT Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was admitted and treated as an inpatient from 04.02.2019 to 09.02.2019 and was diagnosed and underwent surgery,
amputation of right great toe was done on 08.02.2019 which can be made out from Ex.P.6.

entities.text: Gourav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Kolar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.9 for a sum of Rs.1,31,150/-.
There is no contrary evidence against these SCCH - 25 17 MVC No.3870/2020 bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and amputation of right great toe was done.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of HOSMAT Hospital to show the duration and treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least Two months time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.28,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.7/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the petitioner, the petitioner's date of birth is mentioned as 13.12.1976 and the accident occurred on 04.02.2019.
As such, petitioner's age is considered as 42 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 42 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.3870/2020 appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 14.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,29,280/-
(Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 14 x 14%= Rs.3,29,280/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-

sentences.text: The Petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.

He has sustained grievous injuries and amputation of right great toe and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 14%
functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent SCCH - 25 19 MVC No.3870/2020 considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

22. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.60,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.1,31,150/-
3. Loss of income during laid up period Rs.28,000/-
4. Loss of future income Rs.3,29,280/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/-
nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.5,88,430/-
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.5,88,00/- and same is awarded under to the Petitioner.
Liability 23.
The Respondent No.2 has contended that the driver of the JCB did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident.
In order to prove the same, the respondent No.2 got SCCH - 25 20 MVC No.3870/2020 examined Rws.1 & 2 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.4.

RW.1 has deposed in his chief examination that the DL relating to Sri.Ravi D S/o Dhanpal expired on 12.02.2018 and so as on the date of accident i.e., 04.02.2019 the driver did not have valid license to Drive JCB.
The Driver did not get the DL renewed from their office.
Even for renewal in any other office he has to take clearance certificate (CC) from their office.
The Driver has not obtained any CC from their office nor applied seeking for CC.
During the cross examination of RW.1 by the counsel for the petitioner, he has stated that DL for LMV is enough to drive JCB also.
Further admitted he has produced the DL Extract from Sarathi Website.

The badge is valid till 2021 and the badge is issued only on production Manjunatha A.V vs Muniswamy Gowda K.N on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119710520/
8 of valid DL.

sentences.text: 24. RW.2 has deposed in her chief examination that, the data entry operator informed after enquiry that the data for the period of 2018 was not updated.
Hence they have updated the data and issued fresh DL extract as Ex.R.4.
as per the say of the data entry operator some of the data SCCH - 25 21 MVC No.3870/2020 relating to some of the DL holders entered in 2018 was not updated.
They have not given anything in writing to show the same.
During the cross examination of RW.2 by the counsel for Respondent No.2, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
During the cross examination of RW.2 by the counsel for the petitioner, she has stated that the JCB driver had a valid DL to drive a transport vehicle as on the date of accident.
From the evidence of Rws.1 & 2 and the document at Ex.R.4, it is clear that as on the date of accident the driver of the JDB had a valid DL for transport from 14.05.2018 to 13.05.2021.
The date of accident was 04.02.2019.
Therefore, this contention of the Respondent No.2 also does not hold any water.
25. The Respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner himself.
To prove the same it has got examined its official as RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.5 copy of policy.
During the cross examination of RW.3, he has admitted that the reason for SCCH - 25 22 MVC No.3870/2020 delay being in treatment is shown in the complaint.
However, they have not proved their defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.1/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,88,430/-
with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:-

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
 SCCH - 25 23 MVC No.3870/2020  ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,88,430/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Eighty Eight Thousand and Four Hundred and Thirty only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.2 has contended that, the spot of accident was not a public place and it is not liable to pay compensation.
But it is pertinent to refer the decision of full bench of the Madras High Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Parvathi Devi And Ors.
Reported in 1999ACJ1520 SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.3870/2020 and the decision of a Full Bench of the Bombay High Court in Pandurang Chima-ji Agale v. New India Life Insurance Co. Ltd., 1988 ACJ 674, wherein it was observed as follows:
It is also necessary to bear in mind the distinction between the expression 'right of access' and 'access as of right'.
On the other hand, where there is only a right of access,
the owner of the place, if he happens to be a private owner, may deny the access to any members of the public on any ground which he chooses.
In other words, in the former case, the right of the members of the public to use the place is restricted compared to their right to use in the latter case.
The definition under the Act uses the expression 'right of access' as pointed out earlier.
What is, therefore, significant to note is that under the present definition even a place the right to use of which is restricted is a public place.
Therefore, on combined reading of the decisions of full SCCH - 25 12 MVC No.3870/2020 bench of the Hon'ble Madras High Court and Hon'ble Bombay High Court it is clear that even a private place like a factory or agricultural land becomes a public place when the owner permits the public access to the place, leading to right of access to the public even though the said access is not as of right.
